$comment: Bead's metrics: what a registry writes, byte for byte, for what it is given to count, and what each exit of a call or a notification the interop service's server reaches counts, step by step (spec/debugging.md, sections 7 to 12; decision 0013).
mediaType is the media type an exposition is given with (12.1).

An exposition is a registry played on its own. maximumProcedures, where given, is its ceiling (7.4), else its default. routers are the routers it is given, each by its side, client or server, in their order; a declaration or a count names its router by its index among them.

declarations are made in their order (7.2): as is how the procedure is declared, resolver, its resolver registered, notifies true when its procedure notifies; requester, a requester made; notification, a notification registered, on the side that hears. refused, where given, is the reason the declaration is refused (7.3), which declares nothing. serviceRevision, where given, is its service's revision; left out, it is 1.

counts are counted in their order, each on its router. A call, answered or made, is counted whole, from its start to its end, by its outcome, its code when it has one, and its microseconds; one with no outcome started, and is under way. A notification sent or failed counts at the side that notifies, heard at the side that hears; dropped is a subscription dropped at that end, by its code when it has one. A count with no serviceId and procedureId is _OTHER's.
exposition is the text the registry writes then: these lines, each ended by a line feed.

An exit is a conversation of the interop service's server (conversations.json), played as it is, its steps, its limits, its pacing and its relay those of conversations.json, its server given a registry of its own, with its default ceiling, through the option its router takes, metricsRegistry, MetricsRegistry. The server declares to it as it is built: each procedure it offers as a resolver, ticks as one that notifies, and clock, the command it calls, as a requester.

counted is the series that moved since the case began, or since the last counted: each by the line the exposition writes for it, with its value, in the exposition's order; every other series is unmoved, and none is made or gone. It follows a step the server takes, an expect, a report, an advance or a close, and a player reads the exposition on its core's scheduler once the step before it settled. As the case begins, once the server is built, every series is at 0.
A duration is timed on the clock the server is given, which only an advance moves: a call that starts and ends between two advances takes 0 microseconds.
clauses are the units of spec/debugging.md an entry checks: a clause, 7.3; a row of its table, counted from 1, 9.4.2.

exits.name: a result handed to its transport ends its call, its duration in every bucket
a procedure's own failure counts application
a service unknown counts under _OTHER
a procedure unknown counts under _OTHER
a request that names a destination, to a server that relays nothing, counts under _OTHER
a request past the calls its connection has it answer at once counts CAPACITY_EXCEEDED under its procedure, started and ended in one turn
a credential scheme to come counts its procedure's CREDENTIAL_UNSUPPORTED, and a procedure unknown _OTHER's
a credential that does not resolve counts SESSION_REQUIRED
a verifier that fails counts PROCEDURE_FAILED
calls past those let wait for an issuer count CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, each timed from its arrival through its credential's wait
an admission that refuses counts its refusal
an admission that refuses a call in no session counts SESSION_REQUIRED
a transfer its side takes none of counts PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE
a transfer's opening that holds its whole total counts CHUNK_INVALID
a transfer's opening past those its connection receives counts CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, and the transfer under way stays started
a chunk refused ends its request's transfer, CHUNK_INVALID
a chunk past its credit ends its request's transfer, CREDIT_EXCEEDED, and a late one counts nothing
a request's transfer gone silent counts TRANSFER_STALLED, timed from its arrival
a request whose header does not read, of a layout to come, is answered and counts under _OTHER
a malformed request is answered and counts under _OTHER
a request past the envelope's bound is answered and counts under _OTHER
a request on the server's own parity opens no call, and counts nothing
a request on a call id a subscription holds opens no call, and counts nothing
a payload its procedure cannot read counts PAYLOAD_UNDECODABLE
a resolver that fails before it answers counts PROCEDURE_FAILED
a result its side cannot send counts PROCEDURE_FAILED
a subscription refused in its own answer is its call's failure, and drops no subscription
a result sent as a transfer ends its call at its last chunk
a result's transfer stalled before its last chunk counts TRANSFER_STALLED, timed to its failure
a result's transfer cancelled before its last chunk counts cancelled
a result's transfer closed before its last chunk counts closed
a call its requester cancels counts cancelled
a call whose connection closes counts closed
a call awaiting its command as their connection closes counts closed, and the command closed, each once
a command answered counts among the client families, type command, beside the call that made it
a command its client fails counts the failure's code
a command whose answer does not read counts the failure that refused it
a command past its time counts timeout, timed to it
a command whose result's transfer goes silent counts timeout
a relayed call counts under _OTHER in the server families, and its leg B under _OTHER in the client families, type command
a destination's failure counts as answered at both of the relay's gates
a relay's own failure counts under _OTHER, and no leg B

a relay admits by default only a credential it forwards

exits.name: a subscription through a relay counts the relay's SUBSCRIPTION_UNSUPPORTED under _OTHER
a leg B past its destination's timeout counts timeout, and its leg A the relay's DESTINATION_LOST
a leg B whose connection goes counts closed, and its leg A the relay's DESTINATION_LOST
a cancel on leg A counts cancelled at both of the relay's gates
a notification handed to its transport counts sent, under the procedure its subscription went to
a notification a credit lets go from its queue counts sent as it goes, and one queued counts nothing
a client's cancel drops no subscription
a queue past its bounds once answered drops its subscription, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, its notifications queued neither sent nor failed
a session that ends drops its subscriptions, SESSION_REQUIRED
